briefing.headline: The simulation predicts the policy would raise 12-month departures from about 434 to 1,142 out of 5,000 employees, roughly 708 extra leavers and a jump from about 9% to 23% attrition (+175%).
briefing.most_at_risk: Mid-level staff (+230%), caregivers (+219%) and long commuters (+200%) react worst, because three fixed days add hours of travel or clash with care duties, and they are the people with the most to lose and the most options elsewhere; gender makes almost no difference.
risks: The losses concentrate in experienced mid-level staff and managers (+181%), the people who are hardest to replace and who would be expected to enforce the policy.

Badge tracking reviewed with managers comes across as distrust, even among people who can live with three days in the office, so it damages engagement across the whole workforce, not just among those who leave.

Requiring VP approval for exceptions will likely create a backlog and uneven decisions, and caregivers and long commuters are already planning to ask for one; denials could trigger departures within the 90-day window.
design_changes: Drop individual badge reviews with managers, or limit them to anonymous team-level totals, and tie expectations to outcomes. This removes the most-cited 'they don't trust us' grievance at almost no cost.
Let teams pick their own office days and allow managers to grant exceptions against clear published criteria such as care duties or long commutes, with a fast turnaround instead of VP sign-off.

Phase the policy in over a longer period than 90 days, starting with fewer required days, and explain the specific business reason for being in the office so people see it as purposeful rather than arbitrary.
briefing.confidence: low, because the direction is consistent across every group and every voice, but the 1,142 figure rests on only 48 modelled voices (about two per group), and most of them say they will 'start looking' rather than quit, so treat the size of the effect as a warning range rather than a forecast.

subgroup_checks.claim: Bigger rise for mid and senior managers
